punchline: A student living on returned Coke bottles took a calligraphy class with no use, and about ten years later the Mac had proportional fonts.
thirty_sec: Steve Jobs enrolled at Reed College, quit his classes after six months but stayed on campus. He dropped in on a calligraphy class and learned about serif and sans serif type and letter spacing, with no thought of using it. About ten years later, designing the first Macintosh, it all came back. By Jobs's account, without that class the Mac would have had no multiple typefaces. Walter Isaacson tells it in his biography.
